title: A Phone Call About a Stolen Phone
script: Rafi: [panicked] Kak, someone took my phone at the market. I turned around for one second, and it was gone.
Sister: [calmly] Okay, breathe first. Are you safe? That matters more than the phone right now.
Rafi: [shaken] Yes, I'm safe, just shocked. I don't even know what to do first.
Sister: [steady] Good. First, use my phone to log into your account online, and lock the device remotely.
Rafi: [worried] Can someone really open my apps and see my messages, my banking app, everything?
Sister: [reassuring] Not easily, if your screen has a passcode. That's why locking it now matters so much.
Rafi: [regretful] I never set up that remote-lock feature. I always meant to, but I kept putting it off.
Sister: [gently] Many people never do until something like this happens. Let's set it up on your new phone later.
Rafi: [thoughtful] What else should I do right now, before I go to the police?
Sister: [explaining] Change your important passwords, starting with your email and your banking app, just to be careful.
Rafi: [nervous] I'm trying to remember what was saved on that phone. Photos, messages, my whole calendar.
Sister: [warmly] Most of that is probably backed up somewhere, if your cloud backup was turned on.
Rafi: [relieved] I think it was, actually. I remember a message about backup completing last week.
Sister: [encouraging] Good. That's genuinely good news. Photos and contacts are usually the hardest things to lose.
Rafi: [determined] Okay. I'll report it to the police first, then go buy a simple new phone tomorrow.
Sister: [warmly] I'll come with you tomorrow. And next time, please turn on that remote-lock feature immediately.
Rafi: [with a small laugh] I promise. Today taught me that lesson the hard way.
Sister: [gently] These things happen. What matters is you're safe, and we'll sort the rest out together.
